checks: No eclipse at 1 of 20 covered epochs where the 0.89405 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 258151016 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 0.8940 days. Automated analysis of TESS photometry detected a primary eclipse causing 3.87% dimming, with a detection significance of 114.5 in the box-least-squares search. Pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal's location within 0.6 arcsec of the target star, with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 73.4 in difference imaging. No secondary eclipse was detected. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel target. The pipeline's machine-learning model assigned it a screening score of 0.29, and the photometric data passed all quality checks without flagged issues.
